newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Valentino shifts all shows to Paris.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Valentino shifts all shows to Paris.

text.p: Italian fashion designer Valentino said on Wednesday he found Milan depressing and would show all his collections in Paris from now on.

"I'm leaving Milan because the city doesn't inspire me. I don't feel creative there," the stylist told La Repubblica newspaper in an interview from Paris, where designers are this week showing their women's collections for next fall and winter.
"Milan, unfortunately, is a depressing city. I can't bear the atmosphere. It's no longer stimulating. That's why I'm going to work where I feel happier."

Valentino, who had shown his menswear and childrens' collections in Italy's fashion capital but his womenswear in Paris, said he would be sorry to leave Milan, but added: "Rome remains the base of my work. I design all my collections there."

Valentino's decision to leave Milan contrasts with that of other stylists. Romeo Gigli says he is returning after nearly nine years because "Milan is going through a magic time, a little renaissance".
Milan designers showed their autumn/winter collections for women last week to generally favourable reviews.
